item.title: Christopher Kent: Additional monetary policy tools - reflections and a new framework
item.speaker: Christopher Kent

rating.summary: RBA Assistant Governor Christopher Kent introduced the Monetary Policy Board's new Framework for Additional Monetary Policy Tools at low interest rates, drawing on pandemic-era experience and international peers. The framework outlines how the RBA would design, deploy, and exit unconventional tools when the cash rate is very low, though it is explicitly non-prescriptive. Kent emphasized that the cash rate target remains the primary instrument, with additional tools reserved for extraordinary circumstances.
rating.stance_rationale: The speech is forward-looking and procedural in nature, describing a contingency framework rather than signaling any imminent policy shift. There is no directional easing or tightening bias expressed, warranting a neutral score.
key_quotes: The cash rate target remains our primary and preferred instrument for achieving low inflation and full employment.
Additional tools can play an important role during extraordinary times and provide some extra support, but they are more complex and carry greater risks.
